{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance differ across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect or blocking factor in mixed-effects models to account for 8 mice contributing repeated measures",
    "Given unequal sample sizes across paradigms (Combined: 48846, ICMS Only: 11378, Dim Visual Only: 9603, Sham: 3505, Bright Visual Only: 3323), use Type III sums of squares",
    "Check for homogeneity of variance using Levene's test; if violated, use Welch's ANOVA or robust standard errors"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For significant ANOVA results, perform pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD for balanced designs or Games-Howell for unequal variances/sample sizes",
    "For logistic regression on Success, use pairwise odds ratio comparisons with Bonferroni correction",
    "Focus comparisons on Combined vs. single-modality paradigms (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all active paradigms vs. Sham",
    "Estimate Cohen's d or Hedges' g for effect sizes, accounting for unequal sample sizes"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni-Holm step-down procedure across the 5 response variables and 10 pairwise paradigm comparisons (50 tests total), or control False Discovery Rate (FDR) at q=0.05 using Benjamini-Hochberg for greater power given the large sample size",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression is recommended over ordinary linear regression because Stim Paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels. Use the 5 performance variables as predictors to classify stimulation paradigm. Alternative: Random forest or gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) given the large sample size (n=76655) and potential nonlinear relationships. A multinomial model with LASSO regularization can handle multicollinearity among predictors. Evaluate with stratified cross-validation (stratified by Mouse to prevent leakage) and report multiclass log-loss, accuracy, and confusion matrix. If interpretability is prioritized, present odds ratios from the multinomial model with Sham or Combined as reference category.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated by repeated measures from same mice; address via mixed-effects models or cluster-robust standard errors",
    "Normality: Check Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; consider log-transformation for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency given right-skew (max values far exceed means)",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across paradigms; use heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors if violated",
    "Multicollinearity: Examine VIF among predictors for multinomial model; Speed and Path Efficiency may correlate",
    "Complete separation check for logistic/multinomial models given large sample size and potential perfect prediction in some cells",
    "Outlier influence: Check Cook's distance and leverage for extreme AD or Path Efficiency values (max AD=1.0, max Path Efficiency=29.8 vs mean=0.47)"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency) compared to single-modality paradigms based on typical multisensory integration benefits",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only paradigms given direct cortical stimulation, though this is uncertain without prior literature",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance (lowest Success, highest Time-to-Target, lowest Path Efficiency)",
    "Bright Visual Only may differ from Dim Visual Only in speed-accuracy tradeoffs, with uncertain direction",
    "AD (angular dispersion) expected to be lowest for Combined and highest for Sham, reflecting straighter paths with multisensory guidance",
    "Large effect sizes expected for Combined vs. Sham; smaller, potentially nonsignificant differences among active single-modality paradigms after multiple comparison correction"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in paradigm sample sizes (Combined: 63.7% of data vs Bright Visual Only: 4.3%) reduces power for comparisons involving smaller groups and may violate ANOVA assumptions",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure; temporal autocorrelation unaddressed",
    "Mouse-level clustering unmodeled in basic ANOVA; 8 mice with unequal observations (7233-10986) may introduce confounds",
    "Success is binary but treated as numeric in summary; appropriate analysis requires logistic or mixed-effects logistic regression",
    "AD bounded [0,1] and Path Efficiency right-skewed with extreme outliers; standard ANOVA may be inappropriate without transformation",
    "No covariates for difficulty, target distance, or trial type available in supplied data",
    "Temperature=0.0 in metadata suggests deterministic LLM generation; unclear if this affects analysis validity"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response, the 5 performance variables as fixed effects, and random intercepts for Mouse. Use Bayesian estimation with weakly informative priors to handle separation and obtain posterior distributions for paradigm classification probabilities. Complement with permutation-based importance analysis to identify which performance variables most discriminate paradigms, and visualize decision boundaries via LDA or t-SNE projection of the 5-dimensional performance space colored by paradigm."
}
